Title: Single-file TOML/JSON config load with defaults
Detail: Parse one config file (TOML by extension, else JSON) into the Config tree; serde #[serde(default)] supplies zoom_amount/ken_burns defaults so omitting optional fields still loads (SR-003).

Title: Config struct field set with documented defaults/units
Detail: OutputDef/InputConfig/OutputConfig/ProcessingConfig carry every user-facing field (width,height,fps,pic_display_time_secs,fade_time_secs,quality_crf,max_rotation_degrees,zoom_amount,ken_burns,exception_pattern,exception_threshold,max_workers) named in SR-003 Permutations; defaults/units live in the Quick Reference.

Title: Config semantic validation
Detail: Reject media_root-missing, empty outputs, zero dims/fps, crf>51, and duplicate [[outputs]] names (two same-named outputs would silently overwrite one <name>.mp4, breaking SR-017's N-distinct-MP4s criterion) with InvalidConfig messages; this is the config-parse leg of the SR-002 prerequisite gate. Note: does NOT yet emit per-prereq pass/fail lines (see LLR-004).

Title: Runtime-prerequisite checks with per-item plain pass/fail
Detail: run_checks probes each essential RUNTIME prereq separately (FFmpeg via 'ffmpeg -version', ffprobe, Config::validate, media_root readable, output base_dir writable); main::run_validate prints one [PASS]/[FAIL] line each and exit_code/all_essential_passed drive a non-zero exit when any essential check fails. No Rust/build-toolchain check (SR-002). Pure aggregation unit-tested.

Title: Build refuses to start when essential prerequisites fail
Detail: run_build calls preflight::run_checks and, when !all_essential_passed, prints each failing check to stderr and std::process::exit(1) before any media work — no output produced (SR-002, SR-012). Shares the exact LLR-004 check set.

Title: FFmpeg-missing detection with named plain-language error
Detail: Pre-flight check_program spawns 'ffmpeg -version' (and ffprobe) so FFmpeg-not-found is reported as a plain [FAIL] line before processing, for both validate and build (SR-012); FfmpegEncoder::start still surfaces a named spawn-failure error as a backstop.

Title: FFmpeg non-zero exit surfaced as error, no false success
Detail: finish() waits on the child and returns SlideshowError::Ffmpeg with the exit status when ffmpeg fails, so a failed encode never reports success (SR-013). write_frame propagates broken-pipe write errors.

Title: Encode failure names affected output and bounds run time
Detail: FfmpegEncoder arms an inactivity Watchdog (background thread sharing Arc<Mutex<Child>> + AtomicU64 last-activity epoch-ms + AtomicBool finished/killed): write_frame bumps last-activity, the watchdog wakes ~1s and kills ffmpeg once now-last_activity exceeds ffmpeg_timeout_secs (config, serde default 120, 0=disabled), and finish() joins the watchdog and returns a SlideshowError::Ffmpeg naming the output ('encoding timed out for <name>') so a killed run never reports success; Drop still kills+removes the .part on a timeout abort. Pure decision factored as timed_out(last_activity_ms,now_ms,timeout_secs) (0=>false, saturating sub), unit-tested (inactivity_timeout_decision_sr013). Bounds total run to work-time + one timeout interval (SR-013).

Title: Frame-compatible H.264/MP4 encode profile
Detail: Encoder args pin libx264, -pix_fmt yuv420p, -movflags +faststart, -an, and pass -crf through unchanged (SR-005 profile, SR-008 CRF passthrough). Container is mp4 via the .mp4 output path.

Title: Even-dimension enforcement for any configured resolution
Detail: OutputDef::even_dims() returns (width & !1, height & !1) clamped to a minimum of 2, and the pipeline uses it for the encoder dims, frame_bytes, and video reader so odd dims never reach ffmpeg/yuv420p across all SR-006 panel resolutions (SR-005 even-dims, SR-006). Unit-tested (even_dims_rounds_down_sr006, even_dims_never_zero_sr006).

Title: Configurable frame rate honored and default within 24-30
Detail: fps is a configurable field threaded to FfmpegEncoder::start (-framerate) and the Ken Burns frame math (OutputDef::total_frames/fade_frames). The 24-30 default is a documented config value (Quick Reference); validate rejects fps==0 (SR-007).

Title: Quality via CRF passthrough
Detail: quality_crf is passed unchanged as -crf to libx264; validate bounds it to 0-51. The 26-30 default is documented config, not hard-coded (SR-008).

Title: Pre-run/post-run oversize estimate and 3.5GB warning
Detail: estimate_output_bytes(duration,crf) approximates bytes via an assumed CRF->bitrate curve (anchor 8Mbps@CRF23, x0.88/CRF step; documented approximation, ignores resolution/motion); pipeline::warn_if_estimated_oversize computes duration as sum(clip durations) - transitions*fade_time_secs and warns naming the output when est>3.5GB; BuildSummary::oversize_outputs surfaces any FINAL file >3.5GB (path+size) in the summary (SR-009). Unit-tested (estimate_scales_with_duration_sr009, lower_crf_estimates_larger_sr009, oversize_threshold_at_3_5gb_sr009, long_high_quality_run_flags_oversize_sr009).

Title: Source media opened strictly read-only
Detail: Scan/probe only read source (WalkDir + image::image_dimensions + ffprobe; image::open in FrameRenderer::load; ffmpeg decode in VideoFrameReader::open). No code path creates/modifies/moves/deletes under media_root, satisfying SR-010 across build/validate/stats/bench incl. interrupted runs.

Title: Atomic temp-to-final output finalize
Detail: FfmpegEncoder encodes to <name>.mp4.part (forced -f mp4) and finish() std::fs::rename's it to <name>.mp4 only after ffmpeg exits success; on ffmpeg failure, rename failure, or early Drop (kill/panic) it kills ffmpeg and removes the temp, so a killed run leaves no complete-looking final file and re-run is safe (SR-011); ties to disk-full classification leaving no finalized file (SR-015).

Title: Skip-and-continue on unreadable/unsupported input
Detail: Per-clip load errors are logged (path+reason) and skipped via continue; media scan also drops unknown extensions and unprobeable files. Satisfies the skip+continue+log leg of SR-014.

Title: Skipped-count and per-skip reason in completion summary
Detail: record_skip accumulates SkippedInput{path,reason} (deduped by path) and BuildSummary carries them; main::print_completion_summary reports the skipped count + each reason, and run_build exits zero when >=1 output produced, else std::process::exit(1) with a plain 'no outputs produced' message (SR-014).

Title: Disk-full write failure detected and named
Detail: is_disk_full(&io::Error) maps Windows ERROR_DISK_FULL (raw OS 112) / POSIX ENOSPC (28) to true; write_frame, finish-rename, and the dir checks call it and emit disk_full_error ('out of disk space writing <path>') so the failure is named and non-zero, leaving no finalized output via LLR-015 (SR-015). Best-effort; unit-tested (is_disk_full_detects_platform_code_sr015, is_disk_full_rejects_other_errors_sr015).

Title: Output/input path missing-or-unwritable detection
Detail: ensure_dir_exists/ensure_writable_dir name the exact output path and whether it is missing/not-a-dir/unwritable via a write-probe, returning a plain SlideshowError (no panic/stack trace); preflight::check_media_root names a missing/unreadable media_root. Both surface as plain pre-run failures for output base_dir and media_root (SR-016).

Title: Multiple output definitions in one build
Detail: execute() iterates every OutputDef and calls encode_output once each, writing N distinct <name>.mp4 files in one build, each honoring its own width/height/fps/quality_crf (SR-017).

Title: Case-insensitive ignore-pattern exclusion
Detail: is_ignored lowercases each non-empty pattern and the candidate's path RELATIVE to media_root and excludes on substring match anywhere in that relative path — so a pattern can name a file OR a folder (SR-018 target={file,folder}) regardless of case, while a pattern occurring only in the media root's own path never matches (2026-07-17 fix: was file-name-only, which missed the folder target).

Title: Deterministic path-seeded Ken Burns motion
Detail: FNV-1a seed_from_str(path) feeds SplitMix64 SeededRng in ClipPlan::new, fixing zoom direction/pan endpoints/rotation per file so two builds over identical media+config yield identical motion (SR-022).

Title: Per-stage progress reporting during build
Detail: Logs scan totals (run_build) and per-item processed/total + per-output frame throughput during encode. ProgressTracker (src/util/progress.rs) reserved for richer reporting. Covers the progress leg of SR-004.

Title: Completion summary of written outputs (and failures/oversize)
Detail: print_completion_summary lists every written output path + human-readable size, the skipped count + each reason (LLR-017), and any FINAL file >3.5GB with path+size (LLR-013); when zero outputs a plain 'no outputs produced' failure message is emitted and exit is non-zero (SR-004, SR-009).

Title: CI-built make_video_slideshow.exe published to GitHub Releases on tag
Detail: DONE: bin target renamed to make_video_slideshow in Cargo.toml (tests/common CARGO_BIN_EXE_make_video_slideshow updated); .github/workflows/release.yml added (tag v* -> cargo build --release + softprops/action-gh-release uploads make_video_slideshow.exe; FFmpeg NOT bundled, fetched at runtime per LLR-031/SR-027). Actual GitHub Releases publish + clean-no-Rust-host run is Demonstration (verified on a tag push).

Title: In-binary startup self-check + first-run-no-config wizard launch (no standalone setup script)
Detail: DONE: the standalone setup-script model is retired; instead the binary runs an in-process dependency self-check (setup::ensure_ffmpeg, FFmpeg locatable via LLR-032 resolution order) reporting a plain-language path/failure, and main.rs launches the first-run GUI wizard (setup::run_first_run_setup -> LLR-029/030) ONLY when no config exists AND the session is interactive (interaction::should_prompt, LLR-033); non-interactive sessions skip prompt/GUI and fall through to a clean config error (SR-028). No Rust required (SR-024). The interactive self-check + wizard LAUNCH on a clean host remains Demonstration (SR-024 Verification=Demonstration); the gating predicate and config mapping are unit-tested.

Title: End-user download-to-first-slideshow path realized by exe + self-check/wizard + ffmpeg-resolve + config
Detail: The end-user path composes the renamed make_video_slideshow.exe (LLR-025), the startup self-check + first-run GUI wizard (LLR-026/029) which writes a valid config (LLR-030) at the resolved location (LLR-035), FFmpeg resolution/auto-fetch (LLR-031/032), and one build invocation (Commands::Build -> run_build); no manual config edit and no Rust for a basic run. DONE: every composing piece is built — the renamed make_video_slideshow.exe (LLR-025), startup self-check + first-run GUI wizard (LLR-026/029) writing a valid config (LLR-030) at the resolved location (LLR-035), FFmpeg resolution/auto-fetch (LLR-031/032), and the build invocation (Commands::Build -> run_build) are all wired in main.rs. The full download-to-first-slideshow run on a clean no-Rust host remains Demonstration (SR-001 Verification=Demonstration), exercised by the human at the Final gate.

Title: Documentation-realized SRs (capability gaps, quick-reference, audience split)
Detail: SR-019/020/021/025 are Verification=Inspection/Analysis doc requirements already satisfied by the UX-owned docs (Quick Reference §5 marks audio + bulk_video_time_min splitting unimplemented; single quick-reference linked from README; no conflicting restated constraints; End User vs Developer split). Thin tracing LLR only; primary verification is Inspection test cases owned by the Test Engineer.

Title: First-run GUI wizard (PowerShell/WinForms) collects setup inputs
Detail: DONE: src/setup/wizard.rs::run_wizard stages the embedded WinForms script (wizard.ps1, include_str!) to a temp file and runs it under `powershell -STA`, capturing key=value stdout; the script collects source/media path, intermediary/temp video path, frame defaults (resolution, fps, quality), and the number-of-frames (single-vs-multiple) choice, returning the collected values via parse_wizard_output. Pure GUI/collection only — the values→config mapping is the separate LLR-030. Launched only on first run with no config in an interactive session (main.rs gated by interaction::should_prompt; LLR-026/033). GUI dialog verified by Demonstration (SR-026).

Title: Pure wizard-values→valid Config/TOML mapping (unit-testable, no GUI)
Detail: DONE: src/setup/config_builder.rs::build_config is a pure function mapping wizard-collected values (LLR-029) into a Config (even dims, one [[outputs]] per frame named frame / frame-N, sensible defaults for unasked fields); to_toml serializes it and it round-trips via Config::from_file (LLR-001) and passes Config::validate (LLR-003) — each collected field landing in its documented config field; single-frames → one [[outputs]], multiple-frames → multiple. parse_wizard_output reads the wizard key=value stdout and errors on missing required keys (no silent default). Separable from the GUI so the unit tests assert the mapping without driving the wizard (SR-026). Unit-tested.

Title: FFmpeg auto-fetch to per-user dir with offline/use-existing fallback
Detail: ENABLED: fetch_ffmpeg downloads the pinned GyanD/codexffmpeg 7.1 essentials zip (immutable GitHub release) to the per-user cache (%LOCALAPPDATA%/%APPDATA%, no elevation), integrity-verifies it against PINNED_SHA256 BEFORE extraction (LLR-034/SR-029), Expand-Archives it, and places bin/ffmpeg.exe (+ffprobe.exe) in the cache; reuses an existing copy. Offline/blocked fallback = resolve (LLR-032) pointing at PATH/configured FFmpeg; offline-with-none fails loudly (LLR-006/SR-012). Per-user, no admin (SR-027). Demonstrated end-to-end by tests/ffmpeg_fetch.rs (#[ignore], network): downloads/verifies/extracts + runs ffmpeg -version.

Title: FFmpeg resolution-order helper (PATH/configured → per-user cache → fetch)
Detail: PLANNED: a single helper resolving the FFmpeg binary in documented precedence — existing PATH or configured/existing path first, then the per-user auto-fetch cache, then trigger a fetch (LLR-031) when interactive/permitted — returning the resolved path used by validate/build self-check (LLR-026) and FfmpegEncoder::start (LLR-006/009). One resolution point, no duplicated probing (SR-027). DONE: resolve()/pick() in src/ffmpeg/resolve.rs (configured ffmpeg_path -> PATH -> per-user cache), wired into preflight::check_ffmpeg and setup::ensure_ffmpeg; pure pick() unit-tested.

Title: Interactive vs non-interactive gating (never prompt/GUI when non-interactive)
Detail: PLANNED: a single predicate deciding interactivity — TTY/attached-console detection plus honoring --non-interactive and --config <path> flags — that gates every prompt/GUI path (wizard LLR-029, fetch prompt LLR-031). In non-interactive/CI sessions it returns false so the run never shows a GUI and never blocks on input, always completing or exiting non-zero. Critical never-block guardrail for the test harness/CI (SR-028). DONE: is_interactive()/should_prompt() in src/setup/interaction.rs gate the wizard hint (main.rs) and the auto-fetch (setup::ensure_ffmpeg); pure predicates unit-tested across tty/non-interactive/configured states.

Title: Fetched-FFmpeg integrity verification against pinned checksum
Detail: PLANNED: after auto-fetch (LLR-031), compute the downloaded FFmpeg's checksum and compare to a pinned/trusted value recorded in the binary/config before any execution; on match the binary is used, on mismatch/missing/corrupt download it emits a plain-language integrity-failure message, never executes the suspect binary, and aborts non-zero (SR-029). DONE: verify_checksum() (sha2) runs BEFORE the binary path is returned in fetch_ffmpeg; the empty PINNED_URL/PINNED_SHA256 guard hard-refuses so a missing pin cannot silently disable integrity; pinned checksum is a const in the binary, not fetched alongside the download; match/mismatch unit-tested.

Title: Config-write location resolver (beside-exe if writable else %APPDATA%), reported and re-read
Detail: PLANNED: resolve the config path by precedence — beside make_video_slideshow.exe when that directory is writable, else under %APPDATA% — report the chosen path in plain language, and on subsequent runs re-read from the same precedence (beside-exe first, then %APPDATA%) without re-running the wizard. Used by the wizard write (LLR-030) and startup config load (LLR-026/001) (SR-030). DONE: choose_config_dir() (pure) + resolve_config_path() in src/config/location.rs (beside-exe-if-writable else %APPDATA%/<app> else exe fallback), reported in run_validate; pure choice unit-tested across writable/read-only/no-appdata.

Title: Sub-pixel single-warp Ken Burns render (smooth pan/zoom/rotation)
Detail: DONE: ClipPlan::projection(i) builds a floating-point imageproc Projection mapping the pre-scaled source into the render canvas — an eased zoom (crop size render*zmax/zoom, uniform scale zoom/zmax) and focus-anchored float crop origin, composed with a rotation about the render center. FrameRenderer::render_frame feeds it to imageproc::warp_into (Bilinear, sub-pixel) once and center-crops the constant rotation margin to the output size, replacing the old integer crop_imm+resize+rotate that snapped motion to whole pixels (the jitter) and resampled twice. The constant center-crop adds no motion; the existing margin keeps black corners out. Unit-tested: motion_is_subpixel_smooth (fractional per-frame motion, no integer steps) and output_region_stays_inside_source (no black corners under rotation).

Title: Fixed-focus anchoring (per-output default + per-image override)
Detail: DONE: ClipPlan::with_focus(...,Option<(f32,f32)>) sets both pan endpoints equal to a clamped focus (no pan, fixed anchor) when Some, else keeps the default two-point pan; the RNG stream is drawn identically either way so rotation/zoom stay deterministic (SR-022). The focus-anchored crop origin (pre-cw)*f keeps the focus point at a constant screen fraction for all zooms. FrameRenderer::load_with_focus threads the focus to the plan (load() delegates with None). ProcessingConfig.default_focus ([x,y], serde default) supplies a per-output focus for images without an ROI entry. Unit-tested: fixed_focus_holds_a_constant_screen_fraction.

Title: Region-of-interest JSON database load + per-image focus resolution
Detail: DONE: RoiDb parses a JSON map {rel-path: {x,y} | {bbox:[x,y,w,h]}} (serde untagged; bbox-center, clamped to [0,1]); keys and lookups are path-normalized (backslash->slash, leading ./ stripped, lowercased) so Windows paths match. InputConfig.roi_db (serde default) configures the file; main loads it once (a missing/invalid file is a hard error). FrameGenerationPipeline::focus_for keys the image's path relative to media_root, returning the ROI focus if present else ProcessingConfig.default_focus (LLR-037), and passes it to FrameRenderer::load_with_focus. Unit-tested: roi parse/bbox/normalization/clamp/invalid-json and pipeline roi_entry_overrides_default_focus / falls_back_to_default_then_none.

Title: Per-file audio-stream probe (has_audio)
Detail: DONE: process_file sets MediaFile.has_audio; for videos probe_has_audio runs ffprobe (-select_streams a:0 -show_entries stream=codec_type) and is true iff an audio stream exists. Images are always false. A probe failure is treated as no-audio so a quirky file never breaks the build. Drives which clips contribute audio in passthrough (SR-032).

Title: Per-clip output-start capture and audio-delay math
Detail: DONE: encode_output reads CrossfadeMixer::emitted() BEFORE each add_clip — that running output-frame count is the clip's output start frame even through cross-dissolves (the mixer overlaps clips, so it is NOT a naive concatenation). For audio-bearing video clips it records AudioClip{source,start_frame}. ffmpeg::audio::delay_ms(start_frame,fps) converts that to the adelay milliseconds (round-to-nearest), the key to staying in sync (SR-032). Pure delay_ms is unit-tested.

Title: Audio mux pass (adelay/amix/AAC) with atomic finalize split
Detail: DONE: FfmpegEncoder finalize is split — finish_to_part() waits/validates ffmpeg and returns the validated .part without renaming; promote() does the atomic .part->final rename (with disk-full mapping, SR-011/SR-015); finish() = finish_to_part + promote (silent path, used by lib/tests). CrossfadeMixer::finish returns (emitted, part). ffmpeg::audio::mux_audio builds one ffmpeg pass: silent .part as input 0 plus each clip source, per-clip [k:a]aresample=async=1,adelay=ms:all=1, amix(normalize=0,dropout_transition=0)+apad (single clip skips amix), maps 0:v copy + AAC at the configured bitrate/sample_rate, -t = emitted/fps to pin length, +faststart, writes <final>.apart then promotes apart->final and removes the silent part. enable_audio with no audio clips falls back to promote (silent). Per-clip afade audio crossfades noted as a future refinement. Integration-tested end-to-end (ffprobe AAC + duration).

Title: demo.bat + bundled demo config/focus + release-zip packaging
Detail: DONE: demo/demo.bat cd's to its own dir, requires make_video_slideshow.exe beside it (named actionable error + non-zero exit otherwise), creates demo-media/, downloads each pinned Wikimedia Commons (PD/CC0) sample via curl.exe (idempotent — skips an already-present file) and verifies it against a pinned SHA-256 via certutil (mismatch => delete + abort non-zero), then runs `--config demo_config.toml validate` then `build` INTERACTIVELY (no --non-interactive) so a missing FFmpeg auto-fetches per LLR-031/032. .github/workflows/release.yml stages the demo kit FLAT into dist/ beside the exe and uploads make_video_slideshow-<tag>.zip alongside the standalone exe (FFmpeg still NOT bundled, SR-023). The clean-host run is Demonstration (TC-060).

Title: Shipped demo config + focus database are a valid configuration
Detail: DONE: the bundled demo/demo_config.toml loads via Config::from_file (LLR-001) and passes Config::validate (LLR-003) — one [[outputs]] (demo-1280x800, even 1280x800, fps 30, quality_crf 28, enable_audio=true), media_root=demo-media, base_dir=demo-output, roi_db=focus.json, default_focus set — and demo/focus.json loads via RoiDb::load (LLR-038) with a point (cat.jpg) + a bbox (flower.jpg, centre-resolved) entry. tests/demo_assets.rs asserts both so a broken demo kit fails CI rather than an end user hitting it (SR-003 valid-config, SR-031 ROI). Unit/integration-tested.

Title: Per-output audio config fields
Detail: DONE: enable_audio (existing, now honored) gates passthrough; audio_bitrate_kbps (serde default 192) and audio_sample_rate (serde default 48000) feed AudioParams for the AAC encode in mux_audio. Documented in quick-reference with defaults/units; round-trips through TOML. Defaults unit-tested.

Title: Pure encoder arg-list mapping per encoder choice
Detail: New sibling of resolve.rs mirroring the pure pick() pattern (LLR-032): encoder_args(choice, crf, preset) -> Vec<String> returns the -c:v..-movflags arg block consumed by FfmpegEncoder::start (LLR-009). `software` yields today's libx264 args byte-identically; hardware choices map quality_crf to the encoder's control (-cq for h264_nvenc, -global_quality for h264_qsv/h264_amf) and keep -pix_fmt yuv420p, -movflags +faststart, -f mp4, -an so the SR-005 profile fields are invariant across every choice. No I/O; exhaustively unit-testable.

Title: Preflight hardware-encoder probe (listing + 1-frame trial encode)
Detail: probe_encoder(ffmpeg, encoder) runs the resolved FFmpeg (LLR-032) at preflight: `-encoders` listing, then a 1-frame rawvideo trial encode to the null muxer; returns ProbeOutcome{Pass, Fail(reason), Absent}. parse_encoders (pure) extracts the supported-encoder set from the listing text; trial-encode classification is a pure fn over exit status + stderr. Result cached per (ffmpeg, encoder) so a multi-output run (SR-017) probes each encoder once.

Title: Per-output `encoder` config field with validation
Detail: Field lands on OutputDef, not ProcessingConfig: SR-034 requires per-output selection, and it joins the existing per-output encode knobs (quality_crf, audio_*) so one build can target different encoders per output (SR-017). serde default `software` keeps existing configs parsing and the SR-005-verified arg list unchanged. Config::validate rejects values outside the SR-034 set with a plain-language error naming the field and allowed values.

Title: Fallback decision + encoder-in-use reporting
Detail: select_encoder(choice, outcome) (pure) resolves the encoder actually used: auto+Pass -> probed hardware; auto or explicit hardware with Fail/Absent -> software plus a logged WARN naming the encoder and probe reason (never an error — the build proceeds, SR-034). encode_output logs the selected encoder per output ('encoding with h264_nvenc' / 'libx264 (fallback: <reason>)') so run output names the encoder in use.

Title: x264_preset field threaded to software-encoder args
Detail: serde default `medium` yields today's `-preset medium` byte-identically; a configured value passes through encoder_args (LLR-045) on the software path only (hardware encoders have their own preset ladders — out of SR-035 scope). Config::validate rejects values outside the SR-035 set naming the field and allowed values. Quick-reference doc leg owned by UX (SR-020).

Title: Stage-timer instrumentation in the hot path
Detail: StageTimings (new util module) accumulates per-output elapsed for the SR-036 stages. Instrumentation points: FrameRenderer::load_with_focus (decode and prescale timed separately, exposed via LoadTimings — raw time, overlapped with the build since LLR-060), the clip loop's blocking wait on the prefetched renderer (prefetch-stall — the PB-002 numerator, LLR-060), ImageFrameSource::next_frame around render_range (render, one Instant pair per batch), CrossfadeMixer timed_blend/timed_scale (blend), the write_frame call in CrossfadeMixer::emit (encode-write stall), encoder start->finish (ffmpeg-wall). Surfaced as one --verbose log line per stage per output (StageTimings::log_summary), extending the existing end-of-output frames/s line (plan §2); non-verbose output unchanged. BuildSummary.timings carries the per-output OutputTimings snapshot the bench runner (LLR-052) reads. Cheap by design: relaxed u64-nano atomic adds, no syscalls in the frame loop beyond the Instant pairs.

Title: perf-metrics.json writer keyed by PB-ID
Detail: write_perf_metrics(path, pairs) serializes {PB-ID -> number} to docs/test/perf-metrics.json for Scripts/check_perf.py. PB mapping: PB-001 end-to-end frames/s, PB-002 mean clip-boundary stall (LLR-050 boundary-wait timer: the blocking wait on the prefetched clip since LLR-060), PB-003 warm scan s/1k files (cache-served since LLR-059), PB-004 warm-rebuild ratio, PB-005 peak working set. Pure serialization, separable from measurement. Called by the bench path only (LLR-052) — a normal build never writes metrics; an unmeasured PB is omitted and check_perf skips the row; PB-004 is produced by the Scripts/bench.ps1 wrapper (timed build legs, like PB-006), not by the binary.

Title: Bench-corpus runner emitting metrics
Detail: Quiet-host gate: bench.ps1 waits (after the release build) for total CPU < 20% in two consecutive samples 30 s apart before the measured legs — a competing scan/game skews fps rows 10%+ (Round-6b evidence); -SkipQuietWait bypasses, -QuietTimeoutMin (default 30) caps the wait, timeout proceeds with a loud load-suspect warning. The `bench` CLI arm's `--full` mode: a real end-to-end build of the corpus (explicit --corpus, else TestInput/, else synthesized PNGs in a temp dir), scanning cold then warm (probe cache pinned to a fresh temp file per run, so cold is genuinely cold and warm is the SR-038 cache-served number; the user's per-user cache is untouched), capturing the LLR-050 StageTimings snapshot from BuildSummary.timings, computing PB-001 (frames/build-wall), PB-002 (boundary_stall_ms_per_photo), PB-003 (warm scan s/1k files), PB-005 (peak_working_set_mb: Windows K32GetProcessMemoryInfo / Linux VmHWM, omitted elsewhere), PB-004 omitted until SR-037, and writing perf-metrics.json (LLR-051) cwd-relative. Scripts/bench.ps1 is the canonical producer for check_perf: cargo build --release, pinned 1920x1080 bench output config, bench --full, check_perf --tier release; hardware-bound, Tier=Release like SR-013/024/027 TCs.

Title: Pure segment cache-key derivation
Detail: DONE: segment_key (SHA-256 hex over a canonical field-tagged serialization of SegmentKeyInput) hashes the SR-037 key tuple: source path+size+mtime (SourceIdentity; the path is also the Ken Burns seed input, SR-022); the applied ROI focus (pixels change with it, SR-031); encode-relevant OutputDef fields via EncodeParams (even dims, fps, quality_crf, fade/pic times, ken_burns, zoom, rotation, RESOLVED encoder per LLR-047 fallback + x264_preset per LLR-049); left and right neighbor identity (None at album edges); engine version = CARGO_PKG_VERSION + bumpable CACHE_FORMAT_VERSION. combine_keys folds member keys when sub-transition clips merge segments (identity for one member). Pure: any member change yields a new key, bounding invalidation to inserted items plus their two neighbors.

Title: Segment store layout + LRU prune + cache flags
Detail: SegmentStore roots at ProcessingConfig.temp_dir when set, else the per-user cache dir (LLR-031 root). One MPEG-TS file per key (`<key>.ts`: self-contained timestamps, concat-friendly; container VALIDATED by the TC-079 spike 2026-07-18 — h264-in-mpegts concat->mp4 kept frame count, duration, and the SR-005 profile incl. faststart, so the fMP4 fallback is not needed) plus a JSON index (key -> bytes, frames, last-used; and clip_frames records of actual per-clip counts for LLR-055 exactness). lookup validates size on serve; commit renames from a same-volume staging dir; prune_to(cap from ProcessingConfig.segment_cache_gb, default 20 GB, validated positive) evicts least-recently-used; a corrupt/unreadable entry or index is a miss quietly evicted, never failing the build; leftover sweeps are staleness-gated (24h) so a concurrent build sharing the store is never damaged. --no-cache routes the build through the unchanged streaming pipeline (neither reads nor writes); --clear-cache empties the store then proceeds. Cache-on is the SR-037 default build path.

Title: Warm-build segment planner (hit/miss partition)
Detail: DONE: clip_layout is the closed form of CrossfadeMixer's streaming arithmetic (tail p=clamp(c-n,0,n); start E_j=sum(c_i-p_i); boundary at transition midpoint E_j+floor(m/2) iff m=min(p_prev,h)>=1; sub-transition clips hold no tail so they merge into the successor's segment) — pinned to the real mixer by the TC-077 equivalence test so they cannot drift. plan_segments groups clips at boundaries, keys each group (LLR-053/combine_keys), and partitions hit/miss purely given the store's key set. execute_segmented encodes only contiguous miss runs (each run = members + the adjacent context clip per side whose overlap frames are inside the run, via the shared drive_clips + SegmentedEncoderSink), commits by ACTUAL grouping, and re-plans on skip (SR-014) or grouping drift (video estimate wrong) — recorded actual clip_frames make the next plan exact, so the loop converges (bounded, fails loudly). Build summary surfaces reused/re-encoded per output (TC-081 evidence).

Title: Segment encode + concat assembly routed through watchdog + disk-full + atomic promote
Detail: Two halves of the TC-079 spike surface (the Phase-2 foundation). Encode: start_segment reuses the encoder's watchdog/.part/promote machinery with segment_encoder_args — the LLR-045 quality block (shared quality_args, one fact) plus `-f mpegts`, no `-movflags` (MP4-only; applied at assembly); SegmentedEncoderSink rolls to a fresh encoder at each transition midpoint the mixer signals via the FrameSink trait (streaming sink = FfmpegEncoder, roll no-op), so both paths share drive_clips and emit identical frames (SR-022). Assembly: concat_segments runs `ffmpeg -f concat -safe 0 -c copy -movflags +faststart` (stream-copy, no re-encode) writing `<name>.mp4.part`; armed with ffmpeg_timeout_secs via the LLR-008 timed_out decision over part-file growth (concat has no stdin writes to observe); non-zero exit/timeout surface as named SlideshowError with part+list removed (SR-013, no false success); list-write failures map through is_disk_full/disk_full_error (LLR-018, SR-015); the final name appears only via promote() (LLR-015, SR-011). Spike outcome 2026-07-18: .ts segments concat clean (TC-079 green — identical frame count/duration, SR-005 profile incl. faststart, seam windows aligned). Closes the SYSTEM-ENGINEER OBJ-PERF R1 MAJOR finding. Audio mux across the concat timeline landed with LLR-057 (Round 5b); execute_segmented is now the cache-aware default build path (LLR-055).

Title: Audio-delay bookkeeping across the concat timeline
Detail: DONE: on the cached path each audio-bearing video clip's output start frame is the plan's clip_layout start E_j (exact via stored clip_frames actuals) instead of the mixer.emitted() capture; TC-077 asserts the two agree clip-for-clip over a permutation matrix including sub-transition clips, so warm and cold builds mux identical delays (SR-037 warm/cold equivalence). The streaming path keeps LLR-040 unchanged. The AudioClip{source, start_frame} list feeds the unchanged delay_ms + mux_audio (LLR-040/LLR-041) against the concat-assembled .part before the atomic promote (SR-011); end-to-end guarded by the existing TC-057/058/059 suites now routed through the cached default path.

Title: Probe-cache JSON persistence in per-user cache dir
Detail: One JSON file per media_root (name keyed by a hash of the root path) under the per-user cache dir (LLR-031 root) — not beside outputs: media_root is never written (SR-010), and output base_dir is often a removable SD/NAS wiped between runs; the per-user dir survives that and needs no elevation (SR-027 precedent). Entries: rel path -> {size, mtime_ms, kind, dims, duration, has_audio}. load tolerates a missing/corrupt file by starting empty (never fails the scan); save rewrites atomically (tmp + rename, replace-existing). The per-user root is the shared util::file_utils::app_cache_root (one home with LLR-031's ffmpeg dir); MediaLoader::with_probe_cache_path pins the file for tests/bench isolation.

Title: Scan integration: keyed lookup vs re-probe decision
Detail: process_file consults ProbeCache before probing: entry_current(entry, size, mtime) (pure) accepts a hit only when both match; hit -> MediaFile built from the entry with zero ffprobe/header-decode subprocesses; new/changed/corrupt-entry -> probe as today and refresh the entry. Ignore filtering (LLR-021, SR-018) runs before lookup and skip semantics (LLR-016, SR-014) are untouched, so a warm scan's results equal a cold scan's (SR-038). Evidence surface: Album.probe_stats {cache_hits, probed} — TC-085 asserts probed=0 on an unchanged warm scan.

Title: Background clip prefetch with bounded lookahead
Detail: std::thread + sync_channel with lookahead 1-2 (plan §3 1b): while clip N streams, decode+prescale clip N+1 off-thread (FrameRenderer::load_with_focus). The channel carries Result<FrameRenderer> so a failed prefetch is delivered in order to the clip loop, which routes it through the existing record_skip (LLR-016/LLR-017) — SR-014 skip semantics identical to serial. Ken Burns focus (LLR-037/LLR-038) is resolved on the main thread before spawning, so the worker only decodes+prescales. The bounded channel caps memory; boundary-stall reduction is evidenced by the LLR-050 boundary-wait (prefetch-stall) timer: PB-002 counts only the blocking wait on the prefetched result while decode/prescale keep accruing their raw overlapped time (SR-036). Internal restructure, no SR of its own per the R1 no-SR decision.

Title: SIMD resize fast path when rotation is off
Detail: When max_rotation_degrees == 0 the ClipPlan projection is an axis-aligned scale+translate, so render_frame takes a fast path: SIMD resize (fast_image_resize, SSE4/AVX2) of the float crop window instead of generic warp_into; the prescale also moves to SIMD. warp_into remains the rotation path. Determinism stays plan-level per SR-022 (same seed -> same ClipPlan); bit-exactness vs the old resampler is not claimed. Render-timer movement (LLR-050) evidences the gain (SR-036). Plan §3 1c. The crop window is single-homed in ClipPlan::crop_window (shared with projection) so both paths show the identical region.

Title: Fixed-point blend/scale + surplus-head clone removal
Detail: blend/scale rewritten in u16 fixed-point ((a*(256-w) + b*w + 128) >> 8) over chunked slices, rayon-chunked only if still visible in profiles (plan §3 1d); the surplus-head f.clone() in add_clip is removed (consume by value). Weight quantization moves transition bytes at most +-1 LSB; SR-022 determinism (motion parameters) is unaffected. Blend-timer movement (LLR-050) evidences the win (SR-036).

Title: Encoder-writer thread + bounded channels replace batch memory budget
Detail: Per-output stage graph (plan §5): prefetch (LLR-060) -> rayon render pool -> mixer -> EncoderWriter thread that owns ffmpeg stdin, connected by bounded sync_channels (mixer->writer depth ~2x fade_frames). RANGE_MEMORY_BUDGET is deleted; render batches and the mixer->writer channel are both sized by writer_channel_depth (2x fade_frames, floored at 4, byte-capped), so in-flight frame memory is bounded at depth x frame_bytes per buffer (PB-005 guard via LLR-050, SR-036). As built the render pool stays rayon-inside-the-mixer-thread pulling bounded batches; the sync_channels are prefetch->loop (LLR-060) and mixer->writer. CrossfadeMixer's head/tail ring logic is unchanged — only its inputs/outputs become channels. write_frame remains the single watchdog-activity bump point, now on the writer thread (SR-013). Internal restructure, no SR of its own per the R1 no-SR decision.

Title: Cross-thread failure propagation preserves exit/cleanup semantics
Detail: A writer-thread error (disk-full via LLR-018/SR-015, broken pipe, watchdog kill SR-013) is sent back on the result channel and re-raised by EncoderWriter::join in encode_output, so the error path — no false success, non-zero exit, encoder Drop kills ffmpeg and removes the .part (LLR-015, SR-011) — matches the serial behavior exactly; upstream stages unblock via channel disconnect rather than deadlocking.

Title: Build --output filter selects a single output definition
Detail: DONE: `build --output <name>` restricts the run to the one named [[outputs]] definition, resolved up front before any scanning or encoding; an unknown name is a hard InvalidConfig error naming the available definitions (fail fast, never a silent full build). Flag omitted = all definitions build (SR-017 unchanged). Integration-tested.

Title: ClipRenderer trait extraction with shared backend-blind clip loading
Detail: Extract trait ClipRenderer: Send (total_frames; render_range(&mut self, start, end) -> Vec<Vec<u8>>; load_timings) with today's FrameRenderer as the CPU impl; ImageFrameSource holds Box<dyn ClipRenderer> so FrameSource/mixer stay backend-blind. Decode+prescale split into LoadedClip {prescaled Arc<RgbImage>, ClipPlan, LoadTimings}: ClipPrefetcher carries Result<LoadedClip> (LLR-060 ordering/skip-routing/lookahead unchanged) and the consuming clip loop wraps it in the selected backend's renderer — GPU objects never live on the prefetch worker. DESIGN CALL (recorded): prescale stays CPU-side and the GPU uploads the prescaled image — prescale is 1.5% of rot-15 wall (Phase-4a gate evidence 2026-07-18) so GPU-side prescale buys ~nothing; the upload shrinks from a full decode (24MP = 72MB) to pre_w x pre_h (~10-15MB at 1080p); decode+prescale stay single-homed in the prefetcher; and both backends sample identical source pixels, tightening the LLR-073 tolerance.

Title: render_backend config field with validation
Detail: Lands on ProcessingConfig, not OutputDef (recorded call): the wgpu adapter/device is process-wide (LLR-068/069) and one build renders with one backend, unlike SR-034's per-output encoder sessions. serde default auto per the SR-039 default. Config::validate rejects values outside the SR-039 set with a plain-language error naming the field and the allowed values (LLR-047 pattern).

Title: wgpu adapter probe + pure backend-selection decision fn
Detail: Mirror of the LLR-046/LLR-048 encoder pattern: probe_adapter() requests a wgpu adapter (DX12/Vulkan, high-performance preference) and creates the device as the trial step, classifying to AdapterProbe {Present(adapter-name), Absent, Fail(reason)}; the outcome is cached process-wide (OnceLock) so multi-output builds probe once, and the probe runs only when the request could select GPU (render_backend=cpu never touches wgpu). select_backend(request, probe) -> BackendSelection {backend, reason} is a pure decision table realizing exactly the SR-039 selection/fallback AC (cited, not restated; no combination aborts the build); the caller logs the reason/warning and BackendSelection::describe renders the backend-in-use line consumed by LLR-072.

Title: GPU device/queue init + once-per-clip texture upload
Detail: GpuContext (device+queue from the LLR-068 probed adapter; created once per process, pollster-blocked) is shared across clips and outputs. GpuRenderer::new(ctx, LoadedClip) uploads the prescaled image once per clip as an Rgba8Unorm texture (CPU rgb24->rgba expand; wgpu has no 3-byte texel format) with a bilinear clamp-to-edge sampler — hardware bilinear sampling replaces warp_into's CPU resample, the 57.3% rot-15 render share named in the Phase-4a gate evidence. The ~10-15MB upload amortizes over a clip's ~180 frames.

Title: Per-frame textured-quad draw through CPU-computed ClipPlan uniforms
Detail: Per frame the CPU inverts ClipPlan::projection(i) (the same render->source mapping warp_into applies) and composes the constant rotation-margin center-crop offset, uploading one 3x3 matrix as FrameUniforms (bytemuck Pod); the WGSL fragment shader applies that matrix to the fragment position and samples the clip texture — it derives NO motion math, keeping ClipPlan the single source of truth so seeded motion stays backend-independent (SR-022 amendment). The draw targets out_w x out_h directly (margin crop folded into the matrix: no oversized canvas, fewer readback bytes). Within-backend determinism: identical uniforms on one device/driver yield identical draws run-to-run (SR-022 within-backend leg). DESIGN CALL (recorded): Phase-4a scope is render only — crossfade/black-fade stay in the CPU fixed-point CrossfadeMixer (LLR-062), because blending happens AFTER frames leave the FrameSource and folding it into the shader would restructure the mixer/EncoderWriter graph for a 2.6% blend share (gate evidence); revisit only if Phase-4a profiling promotes blend.

Title: Staging-buffer readback ring emitting unchanged rgb24 frames
Detail: 3-deep ring of mappable staging buffers: frame i's copy_texture_to_buffer + async map overlap frames i+1/i+2's draws; on map completion the CPU strips the 256-byte-aligned bytes_per_row padding and the alpha byte into a Vec<u8> rgb24 frame identical in shape to the CPU path, so FrameSource/CrossfadeMixer/EncoderWriter and every downstream invariant SR-039 cites are untouched. Depth 3 caps readback staging memory at 3 x out_w*out_h*4. Readback bandwidth is a non-issue at target resolutions (plan section 6: ~0.8GB/s vs 16-25GB/s PCIe); the 21.6% rgb24 stdin pipe-write share (12.5GB per canonical build, gate evidence) is explicitly OUT of Phase-4a scope — the recorded Phase-4b boundary.

Title: Runtime fallback, device-lost degrade, backend-in-use reporting
Detail: Startup: encode_output logs the LLR-068 selection (rendering with gpu (<adapter>) / cpu (fallback: <reason>)) — the SR-039 reporting leg, mirroring LLR-048's encoder-in-use line. DESIGN CALL (recorded) — device lost mid-build: GpuRenderer retains its LoadedClip (prescale + plan), so on a device-loss error it completes the in-flight range on a CPU FrameRenderer built from that SAME LoadedClip (identical crop_window/projection — seam-free within the LLR-073 tolerance), logs one warning naming the loss reason, and sets a process-wide degraded flag so every later clip selects CPU without re-probing. Chosen over record_skip: SR-039's never-fail clause promises a complete build when only the GPU is lost and the source media is fine — SR-014 skip semantics stay reserved for unreadable input.

Title: Cross-backend tolerance comparison helper
Detail: Pure fn over two equal-length rgb24 buffers returning the mean absolute per-channel difference (f64) — the hook the SR-039 cross-backend Demonstration leg and the Round-7c TCs assert against; the epsilon lives in the verifying TC row, not here (one home). Sits beside the renderers so unit tests, integration tests, and the bench comparison leg share one implementation instead of three ad-hoc diffs.

Title: New dependencies wgpu + bytemuck + pollster
Detail: wgpu: safe Rust over DX12/Vulkan (per-machine adapter pick, no SDK/toolchain for end users — the plan section 7 rejection of raw Vulkan/CUDA stands); bytemuck: Pod casts for FrameUniforms and staging-buffer reads; pollster: minimal block_on for wgpu's async adapter/device/map calls (no tokio runtime). Honest cost, recorded: wgpu is the heaviest dep in the tree (~150 transitive crates incl. the naga shader compiler; clean release build roughly +1-2 min; binary expected +4-8MB) — accepted against removing the 57.3% rot-15 render share (gate evidence); features trimmed to dx12+vulkan (no GLES/Metal/WebGPU) to cap compile time and size.
